sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Affinities** are a mechanic in Elden Ring that alters a weapon's properties after applying Ashes of War.

sections.heading: Mechanics
sections.markdown:
All Affinities except for Standard, Heavy, Keen, and Quality (the "basic four") will prevent Weapon Buffs from being applied to a weapon (except for those applied via a skill), and will also limit the amount of compatible skills.
- More specifically:
 - Magic and Cold skills and affinities are only compatible with affinities and skills of the "basic four" affinities or those of Magic or Cold affinity.
 - Fire and Flame Art skills and affinities are only compatible with affinities and skills of the "basic four" affinities or those of Fire or Flame Art affinity.
 - Lightning and Sacred skills and affinities are only compatible with affinities and skills of the "basic four" affinities or those of Lightning or Sacred affinity.
 - Poison, Blood, and Occult skills and affinities are only compatible with affinities and skills of the "basic four" affinities or those of Poison, Blood, or Occult affinity.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown:
Standard** is an affinity in Elden Ring.

This is the default affinity of all infusable weapons except for the Butchering Knife, which is Sacred by default. It provides a weapon's default scaling modifiers, a mix of Strength-scaling and Dexterity-scaling.

The Standard Affinity is compatible with all Skills by default, even without any of the Whetblades. It is the affinity of all Ashes of War exclusive to ranged weapons (Light Bows, Bows, and Greatbows), and to Perfume Bottles Shadow of the Erdtree and Hand-to-Hand Shadow of the Erdtree weapons.

It's also the affinity of the vast majority of shield and parry Ash of Wars (mostly exclusive to Small Shields, Medium Shields, Greatshields, and Thrusting Shields, though the latter two cannot accept parry-based ashes) except for Ash of War: Carian Retaliation and Ash of War: Thops's Barrier (both Magic affinity), and Ash of War: Golden Parry, Ash of War: Holy Ground, and Ash of War: Vow of the Indomitable (all three Sacred affinity).

sections.heading: Locked weapons
sections.markdown:
A few weapons are upgraded with regular Smithing Stones but cannot have their affinity changed from Standard.

These include the Crystal Knife and Ivory Sickle Daggers, the Ripple Blade Axe, the Troll's Hammer Colossal Weapon, the Treespear Great Spear, and the Ripple Crescent Halberd Halberd.

sections.heading: Bullet skill-scaling
sections.markdown: For any skill with damage separate from the weapon itself, such as Skill: Beast's Roar and Skill: Flame of the Redmanes, it provides neutral scaling for Intelligence-, Faith-, and Arcane-scaling skills but slightly decreased scaling for Strength- and Dexterity-scaling skills.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Arena Combat** is a mode where players can compete against other players in ritual combat. There are different modes and venues to chose from and the more Victories a player claims, the higher they'll increase in rank, though there are currently no practical rewards for competing in Arena Combat. Players have some control of whom they can connect with through the use of passwords.

sections.heading: Colosseums
sections.markdown:
There are three colosseums scattered across the Lands Between, each provide their own mode, their own respective venue to fight in and each venue has it's own music track playing in the background.

After interacting with each colosseum's respective registration altar, players can freely access each venue and each mode from the Roundtable Hold by interacting with Marika's Effigy, it is found next to the fireplace in the same room as the Table of Lost Grace.

sections.heading: Arena Ranks
sections.markdown:
Each Colosseum have ranks that track the results of combatants for Duels, United Combat/Combat Ordeal and Spirit Ashes allowed.
There are five ranks for each mode. A combatant's rank will be displayed next to their character's name, it can also be found outside of combat, in the Arena's lobby menu.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **ancient ruins** (古遺跡, *Furui Iseki*), also known as **giant ruins** (巨大な古遺, *Kyodai na Furui Iseki*), are recurring structures found throughout the Lands Between in Elden Ring. They were seemingly built by the ancient civilization associated with the ruins at **Rauh** (ラウフ, *Rau**fu**,* possibly *Lauf*).

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown: The ancient ruins are enormous megastructures scattered throughout and incorporated into the Lands Between. They typically consist of repeating octagonal pillars and arches made from black stone that is generally darker than the surrounding natural rock formations. Many of these ruins are so deeply embedded within the earth that they seem to predate the very lands above them, suggesting that parts of the Lands Between rest atop artificial platforms. Though the Ancient Ruins of Rauh are the most intact of these structures, other examples are found throughout Limgrave, Caelid, and the Mountaintops of the Giants, within the Ruin-Strewn Precipice, and at the Rauh Base. The Divine Towers and even the pillar that the Forge of the Giants rests upon use the same architectural style.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
The ancient ruins are remnants of a prehistoric empire that spanned the entire Lands Between. The Rauh civilization predated the hornsent and was one of the earliest in the realm, rivalling the Ancient Dynasty and Farum Azula. According to hornsent scholars, the inhabitants of Rauh practised a form of spiritual manipulation, with their most well-known artifact being the Spritestone, which could manipulate the moment when a spirit vanished. These were crafted from Rauh Burrows, stones with small, nest-like holes meant to be inhabited by tiny spirits called 'sprites', enabling them to function as ritual implements. The Rauh people also used Dewgems as an ingredient in sprite medicine. These secrets were thought lost to time until their rediscovery at Rauh by hornsent archaeologists.

Statues of a mysterious woman with a great octagonal crown are prominently featured throughout the Ancient Ruins of Rauh. Both the hornsent and Kindred of Rot offer their prayers to this goddess-like figure. The Verdigris Discus can be found under one of these statues. The Antiquity Scholar's Cookbook 2 and the Bondstone are located beneath another, held by the corpse of a hornsent. In addition, female figures with pointed headpieces and long side veils are represented in other artistic reliefs at the Rauh ruins.

sections.heading: Locations
sections.markdown:
- Highroad Cave — a Guardian Golem protects black stone structures buried in the earth. These structures are built at the junction where the inland sea meets the Murkwater river that runs south through Agheel Lake and feeds into the sea via another set of Rauh arches.

- Limgrave — structures are found along the southwest coast of Limgrave, bridging the chasm that separates the region from the Weeping Peninsula.

- Weeping Peninsula — a row of black stone structures cross through Tombsward Ruins in western Weeping Peninsula.

- Wailing Dunes — large arches of black stone emerge from the plateau, running east into the sea. This structure was likely once continuous with the corresponding sections at the Mohgwyn Palace deep underground.

- Ruin-Strewn Precipice — appears to be a great dam positioned at the point where the Altus Plateau meets Liurnia of the Lakes. It is connected to the Seethewater river, which originates in Gelmir and floods the lower region.

- Mountaintops of the Giants — black stone megastructures are present along the stretch of the frozen river that crosses the Mountaintops of the Giants and a valley in the Consecrated Snowfield where a large number of Guardian Golems protect it.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- The Rauh civilization created colossal golems from stone and lava. These Guardian Golems are commonly found near their ruins. Their great arrows are imbued with ancient magic and generate tempestuous gusts of wind.
- Flowing water is a persistent motif in the Ancient Ruins of Rauh. The location features numerous Dewgems and waterfalls, and irrigation channels bisect its paved roadways.
 - The Guardian Golem at Highroad Cave drops the Blue Dancer Charm related to the blind swordsman who defeated the ancient rot god.
 - The giant stone arches may have been constructed to divert rivers or regulate water flow, possibly to mitigate the impact of erosion or prevent the accumulation of stagnant water.
- The Rauh civilization used heftiness to represent the burden of the strong to protect others.
 - "Heft" was later used to describe the Giant's Red Braid, Thorned Whip, Prelate's Inferno Crozier, and Giant-Crusher, among others. The Fire Prelates, who revered the Fire Giant, used heftiness to symbolize the weight of their duty. Many Fire Monks later abandoned their posts to serve the "weighty" Black Flame.
- Rauh is internally referred to as モヘンジョダロ, *Mohenjo-Daro*, an ancient ruin of the real-world Indus Valley Civilization, one of the earliest cities ever built.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **ancient dynasty** was a faction mentioned in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.markdown: Ancient dynastic ruins are white stone structures with rectangular floorplans and simple rounded columns with square pedestals and Corinthian capitals. The dynasty produced a large variety of obelisks and other stelae depicting trees, beasts, and seated ancestors. Other artifacts featured stone coffin arks and bulls bearing great rings upon their backs. The ancient dynasty erected countless statues of a one-eyed, bearded elder clutching a stone tablet engraved with a tree, while another bearing a sun or star-shaped map lay discarded at his feet.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
In times of old, long before the age of the Erdtree, a great tree-tending dynasty flourished in the Lands Between. They emphasized ancestor observation and the cultivation of trees, and venerated a bearded elder who discarded one of two stone tablets. Their civilization constructed significant landmarks along the banks of the Siofra and Ainsel Rivers, such as the Grand Cloister, Uld Palace Ruins, and Mohgwyn Palace.

The ancient dynasty documented the enormous stone coffins that washed ashore the Cerulean Coast, arriving since the era when Death was burned in ghostflame. The vessels featured pallbearers, statues of the dynastic god, and heroic scenes, though the tainted heroes interred within had congealed into a putrescent liquor. The remains were given equal treatment in death by the Deathbirds, until the practice ended.

Claymen armed with blue glowing weapons fashioned from sharpened meteoric ore served the ancient dynasty. These priests searched for revelations on behalf of their masters, casting magical bubble sorceries. They once received oracles through their bubbles.

The ancient dynasty eventually collapsed, buried in the lightless depths deep underground. Their ancient bowers petrified, turning to stone. Despite their masters' absence, the Claymen priests—warped and bowed with age—continued searching their bubbles for lost oracles as the world carried on without them.

The dynastic ruins were later inhabited by Ancestral Followers and Kindred of Rot. During the Shattering, Luminary Mohg sought to establish his own Mohgwyn Dynasty at the Mohgwyn Palace.

sections.heading: Members
sections.markdown:
- Bearded Ancient Dynasty Statue, clutching a tablet
- Clayman
- Putrescent Knight
- Putrescent Rotmound
- Putrescent Skeleton

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- The one-eyed Bearded Elder presumably founded the dynasty. His statues are found on stone coffins and in the ruins of dynastic sites. None of the Hallowhorn Grounds in the Siofra River area contains bearded elder statues; instead, they venerate hallowed Horned Remains of long-lived stags.
- Their use of fishing equipment like Clayman's Harpoon indicates they lived along a body of water.
- The dynasty either arrived in the Lands Between in the stone coffins or sent them off to sea. Claymen either formed from putrescence or became putrescent over the ages, respectively.
- The Claymen priests presumably search for Oracle Envoys, whose appearance heralds the arrival of a new god or age. Oracle Envoys blow into golden horns to produce music and golden bubble magic. The Envoy's Greathorn casts Unique Skill: Great Oracular Bubble, which has the same title as the Great Oracular Bubble spell cast by Claymen.
 - They likely also search for Metyr, Mother of Fingers, who communicated with the Greater Will through her bubble-like microcosm before she was broken and went into hiding long ago.
 - Ancestral Followers use Greathorn Hammers and Winged Greathorns in their rituals, linking the term to ancient dynastic sites.
- Ancient dynasty ruins stood above ground in the past because they grew trees, and the "lightless depths" are their grave. They may have had a long-forgotten conflict with Astels, as they used meteorites and an Alabaster Lord and Withered Astel dwell within the Lake of Rot and Uhl Palace Ruins (south), respectively. Astel, Naturalborn of the Void (grace) can only be reached by descending the waterfall at the Grand Cloister and traveling further downstream. It's also possible the ruins were buried at the same time as the nearby Eternal Cities.
- The obelisk scenes with the elder reaching into the branches of the tree to present something to a maiden also appear at the center of Erdtree Greatshields, carried by the Tree Sentinels. The Erdtree Greatshield condenses two frames into a single image, depicting an elder and a maiden beside a tree. The elder reaches his right arm into the boughs, his left hand resting on the pommel of a sword that serves as a cane.
- The Four Belfries bear carvings of the Bearded Elder emerging from leafless branches. These structures are more architecturally sophisticated than those of the ancient dynasty.
- The Suppressing Pillar uses ancient dynasty architecture.
- Miranda Blossoms are sometimes found in their ruins.

sections.markdown: Ancient Dragon Senessax** is an optional boss in Shadow of the Erdtree encountered inside the Jagged Peak.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown: An ancient dragon that can be found sleeping at Jagged Peak, Senessax is implied to have sided with Bayle the Dread, as some of the ancient dragons who betrayed their lord Placidusax to side with Bayle were known to wield branching red lightning.

sections.heading: Appearance

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Ancient Dragon Cult**, also simply known as the **Dragon Cult**, is a faction in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown: The ancient dragon cult is devoted to the worship of the ancient dragons. The religion plays a deep, long-standing role in the history of the Beastmen of Farum Azula, while its practice amongst humans was established more recently. The cult was based in Leyndell, Royal Capital, and championed by Godwyn the Golden in collaboration with Ancient Dragon Lansseax and Dread Fortissax after the conclusion of the war between Leyndell and the Ancient Dragons. Its equipment and incantations heavily base themselves on the Ancient Dragons and emulate their ability to conjure lightning.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
The gold-worshipping capital of Leyndell was attacked by a legion of Ancient Dragons, led by the colossal Ancient Dragon Gransax. Gransax's assault would be the only time in the historical record that Leyndell's walls had fallen and marked the dawn of the war against the ancient dragons. This brutal war ended with Godwyn's triumph over and immediate peacemaking with Ancient Dragon Fortissax.

The implementation of the faith in Leyndell would be supported largely by the arguement that the worshipping of the ancient dragons did not clash with belief in the Erdtree, as the very scales of the ancient dragons, and lightning itself, were both imbued with gold. Ancient Dragon Lansseax, sister of Fortissax, assumed the form of a humanoid priestess to teach the blessings of the Ancient Dragons to Leyndell's inhabitants, bolstering its defenses with lightning.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
The Age of the Duskborn represents a potential future for the Lands Between in which the Rune of Death is restored to the Elden Ring by the Elden Lord. This allows for the integration of Those Who Live in Death into the Golden Order.

This is made possible through the Mending Rune of the Death-Prince gestated by Fia, Deathbed Companion, after transferring her accumulated heroic lifeforce to the Prince of Death—the soulless body of Godwyn the Golden.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Age of the Stars** is one of the possible endings in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
The "Age of the Stars" ending sees The Tarnished aid Ranni the Witch in ousting Marika and remaining at her side as Ranni's first Elden Lord.

The Tarnished helps Ranni fulfill her vision of a Lands Between without the Golden Order by allowing her to replace Marika in godhood and takes the role of her consort. Ranni ushers in a new order not of gold, but of the stars and moon of the chill night. Rather than make herself and her order objects of worship, she chooses instead to keep her order and the Lands Between at a great divide, removing the certainties of faith that had existed during Marika's rule.

The Tarnished and Ranni leave the Lands Between, embarking on a thousand-year voyage into darkness under the wisdom of the Dark Moon. Even if life and souls are one with the order, it will be out of sight, emotion, faith, and touch.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Ancient Dragon-Man** is an Invader and optional Enemy boss in Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
The Ancient Dragon-Man is enountered twice in the Gravesite Plain—once as an Invader and once as a formal boss. His Invasion triggers on the road southwest of the Pillar Path Waypoint Site of Grace. He is fought up the hill past Igon, who audibly cowers on the ground. The boss version is encountered at the bottom of the Dragon's Pit. Defeating him opens the path to the Foot of the Jagged Peak, which connects to Charo's Hidden Grave and the Jagged Peak.

Formerly a drake warrior who hunted colossal dragons, the Ancient Dragon-Man partook in the original form of Dragon Communion by consuming a jagged Rock Heart. He took on the stony form of a small, bipedal ancient dragon and became the arbiter of those worthy to devour Bayle the Dread.

sections.heading: Moveset
sections.markdown:
- Wields the Dragon-Hunter's Great Katana and Dragon Communion Seal.
- Uses the Magma Breath and Dragonmaw Incantations.
- Prefers two-handed jumping attacks and Dragonwound Slash.
- Has transformed using a Rock Heart.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Ancient Dragon-Man has a single Flask of Crimson Tears.
- He has 0 Poise and 0% Damage Negation for each Damage Type.
- Draconic Tree Sentinels also became dragons to better fight dragons.

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.markdown:
It is possible to defeat the Ancient Dragon-Man without having leveled up or upgraded one's Weapons, Flasks and even Scadutree Blessings with relative comfort through the use of spamming the crouching light attack from Whips. As its long reach, fast attack-speed, low stamina-consumption and early stamina-regeneration, combined with the Ancient Dragon-Man's non-existent poise, allows the player to consistently harass him from a relatively safe distance without needing to worry about him trying to excessively dodge and then rush the player down like conventional projectiles from spells or bows would.

The player can increase their un-upgraded weapon's damage-output through the use of Blood Loss, Frostbite and Poison procs that are then immediately followed by the use of the Skill, The Poison Flower Blooms Twice as a third source of blood loss-like burst-damage.

The most efficient set-up for this would be to have two different whips they can alternate between. Hoslow's Petal Whip and Thorned Whip are excellent choices as they can both have their Affinities changed through the use of Ashes of War, while at the same time preserving their innate blood loss buildup no matter what affinity is chosen. So one Poison whip with Ash of War: The Poison Flower Blooms Twice and a Cold whip with almost any ash of the user's choosing.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Ancient Ruins of Rauh** (ラウフの古遺跡, *Rau**fu*** *no Furui Iseki*, possibly Lauf), also known as the **Rauh Ruins**, is a subregion of the Realm of Shadow in Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
The Ancient Ruins of Rauh is an area defined by verdant life and flowing water. It features numerous waterfalls and pools where Dewgems grow in abundance, and its paved roadways are bisected by irrigation channels. This massive stone complex was once part of a ancient civilization that spanned the entire Lands Between, but it has since flooded, split in half, and became overgrown with plants and wildlife.

The Ancient Ruins of Rauh is perched high above the Rauh Base, and connected via bridge to the Shadow Keep in the east. It comprises the upper section of the Rauh Ruins, located within the Land of the Tower.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
The ancient Rauh civilization predated the hornsent, and rivaled the Ancient Dynasty and Farum Azula as one of the earliest cultures to emerge in the Lands Between. The primordial Crucible of life flourished and likely originated in Rauh, and, according to legend, the "mother of all Crucibles" first appeared on the Giants. Its influence mutated the local wildlife to grow aspects of other creatures, such as horns and feathers. The area was suffused with such potent spirituality that an acrid Spirit Calculus formed on its inhabitants over time.

According to hornsent scholars, the inhabitants of Rauh practiced a form of spiritual manipulation. Their most well-known artifact was the Spritestone, also known as "bondstone," which could manipulate the moment when a spirit vanished. These spritestones were crafted using Rauh Burrows, oval-shaped stones modeled with small, nest-like holes at their center to be inhabited by spirits, enabling them to function as ritual implements. Bondstones were large burrowstones with a white gem obtained from polishing a special crystal. These were used to control the explosions of spiritual powers, thus determining the moment when the bond with the spirit would be broken.

For unknown reasons, the civilization of Rauh collapsed, and the city fell into ruin. It was split in two by a great chasm and became flooded and densely overgrown with vegetation. The secrets of spiritual bonding were lost to time.

sections.heading: Hornsent
sections.markdown: After their rise to power, the hornsent made expeditions to the Rauh ruins. They sought to understand the secrets of antiquity because these ruins were strongly associated with the Crucible that they held sacred. They erected the Church of the Bud in the Rauh ruins. The structure was known for its flowers and featured a large ornamental bud and stone platform for viewing adjacent Belurat and Enir-Ilim. Whether intentional or not, it was constructed atop a divine element. Later, hornsent archaeologists rediscovered the process for making spritestones and other forgotten spiritual arts.

sections.heading: Age of the Erdtree
sections.markdown:
During Messmer's Crusade, his army marched toward Enir-Ilim through the ruins of Rauh. They razed the Church of the Bud and installed the Sealing Tree on the stone platform. However, the ruins were preserved due to the intervention of Fire Knight Salza, who defied orders to burn them. Messmer's forces collected large horned beasts and tanglehorned giants from the ruins for the Specimen Storehouse instead.

As the Church of the Bud burned around her, Romina sat on the ground, clutching the bud in speechless silence. She discovered a twisted divine element in the ashes and modified it into the scarlet rot. After the Battle of Aeonia, Romina summoned and soothed Malenia's unwanted butterflies, who allowed her to practice an ancient purification ritual once lost to time. Her actions imbued the church's flowers with scarlet rot, caused local Spider Scorpions to grow in size, and transformed the landscape surrounding the Church of the Bud into a scarlet rot swamp.

sections.heading: Game events
sections.markdown: The ruins are a lush oasis of green in the dour Realm of Shadow. Their sanctity is ensured by Fire Knight Salza, who guards the west entrance to the city. The eastern section of the complex is home to many Bloodfiends and horned beasts. The subterranean structures are excavated by Shadow Undead in search of the secrets of Rauh. The western half of the ruins are dominated by a Servants of Rot cult led by Romina, Saint of the Bud. The waters in this section are stagnant, festering pools of rot. Like the Scarlet Buds of the Church, the bodies of the Kindred of Rot have turned bright scarlet, indicating their acceptance by Romina. The ruins are also home to many Spider Scorpions and other creatures touched by the Crucible.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Ancient Dragon Gransax** was a character in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown: Gransax was an enormous ancient dragon who wielded a great spear modeled after a spiraling bolt of yellow lightning.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown: During the early Age of the Erdtree, Gransax attacked Leyndell, breaching the walls of the Royal Capital and triggered the War of the Ancient Dragons. During his assault, the knights of the Erdtree employed Golden Lightning Fortification, an Erdtree Worship incantation, to shield themselves from his red lightning. Gransax was ultimately defeated, frozen in place at the Fortified Manor. In the aftermath, a faction of Tree Sentinels concluded that the only way to protect the Erdtree was to transform into dragons themselves, becoming the malformed Draconic Tree Sentinels.

sections.heading: Location
sections.markdown: The Gransax's immense stone body lies where he fell in Leyndell, Royal Capital, at the Fortified Manor.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- It is unclear what exactly prompted Gransax and the ancient dragons to descend from Farum Azula and attack the Royal Capital.
- Gransax is approximately 328 meters in length—nine times larger than the standard ancient dragon.
- Gransax's body is partially buried in ash in Leyndell, Ashen Capital.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- The Bolt of Gransax is one of the legendary armaments required for the achievement.
- Gransax (~328m) dethroned the Dragon God (182m) from *Demon's Souls* as the largest dragon in a FromSoftware game. However, with the release of Shadow of the Erdtree, Gransax lost this title to the colossal drake (~392m) located at the Grand Altar of Dragon Communion.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **ancestral followers**, also known as the **horned folk**, are a faction in Elden Ring. They reject the advancements of society and worship the ancestral spirits.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.markdown:
The blue-eyed ancestral followers are robust, brawny humanoids with bluish, bruise-colored skin and silvery gray hair. Their muscular bodies outsize their heads and their faces are brightly painted white with red designs. While they do not exhibit the natural horn growth they venerate, they emulate its presence with headbands.

The horned folk do little to modify what nature had given them, using minimally-procesed organic materials like bone and animal pelts for their weapons and attire.Their great horned headbands were spoils harvested from dead beasts. Warriors carry hefty weapons imbued with ancient spiritual power, taken from the remains of herbivorious beasts. They do not sharpen their crushing jawbone axes and their arrows capitalize on the natural puncturing ability of animal fangs.

They wear protective necklaces and horn charms to boost their focus and ward off disease and other maladies. Mottled accrouments with vivid and varied coloration are most precious to the followers. The Shamans wear Shining Horned Headbands adorned with fingerprint talismans, likely made from putrescence or Silver Tears.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
The horned folk rejected writing and metalworking in all its forms, living in primitive hunter-gatherer communities among dynastic ruins and ancient bowers. They worshipped the spirits of herbivorous beasts, a deeply-rooted faith that operated beyond the purview of Marika's Golden Order. They distanced themselves from the Erdtree, waiting for new buds to sprout in the Lands Between. 

The horned folk recognized Death as a means to gain power. They knew life sprung forth from both birth and death, and that it could bud from their very souls. They revered the radiant antlers of long-lived stags, from which which new life blossomed endlessly until the beast became an Ancestor Spirit.

The rituals of the followers tapped into the spiritual energy that dwelled within the bones of beasts. In these ceremonies, they stamped their feet in syncopation with a beautiful lullaby sung by exalted shamans. The head of an ancestral infant was swung like a censer to produce a mist of blue spirit vapor that sapped souls and siphoned vitality. Any life that showed no signs of budding was culled in the miasma by warriors wielding greathorns that resembled the wings of an envoy.

The ancestral followers were master hunters who shared a bond with beasts. Normally timid creatures, such as deer and sheep, remained unafraid in their presence. Many animals accompanied them as they foraged through the wooded areas. Living in idyllic harmony with herbivorous creatures, they made their home among the underground ruins of the ancient dynasty along the banks of the Siofra River.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- The ancestral followers near the Hallowhorn Grounds (South) are spectral and glow with blue light. They are invisible to those far away.
 - The blood of the ancestral followers is red, however, the blue spirit followers bleed white.
- The song of the shamans draws blue spirit energy into the bodies of nearby followers. The horns of those who hear it siphon spirit energy and illuminate with blue light whenever the follower damages an enemy.
- It can be inferred that they value the Crucible due to their reverence for horns and the spiral.
 - Their practices are similar to the Horn-Calling of the Horned Warriors, but they seem to focus on imbuing the horns with power instead.
 - The ancestral followers once cultivated close ties with a Tarnished and gifted them a Spiralhorn Shield.
 - Despite their indifference the Erdtree, they pray towards the Minor Erdtree in east Liurnia; the local Erdtree Avatar does not attack them.
- The followers distanced themselves from gold, silver, and the ancient smithery, rejecting metalworking altogether.
- The winged greathorn ritual implement is selected for its resemblance to a life-reaping winged envoy.
 - Like Lichdragon Fortissax, this design may echo the wings of the Death Rite Birds. The greathorn hammer vaguely resembles the winged scythe, which is said to depict white-winged maidens, who are also messengers of Death.
- The ancestral shamans cradle an infant in their arms, similar to the Abductor Virgins, catacombs sorcerers, the twinned armor, the Gloam-Eyed Queen, and the statue of Marika in the Shadow Keep.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
The age of the Elden Ring likely refers to an era of Golden Order Fundamentalism spearheaded by Queen Marika the Eternal and her second Elden Lord, King Consort Radagon. This era was marked by worship of the Golden Order and its key fundamentals—the Law of Causality and the Law of Regression.

The cursed twin Demigods Miquella and Malenia were born during this time.

This era ended when Marika shattered the Elden Ring, triggering the Shattering.

sections.markdown:
- Alternatively, the "age of the Elden Ring" may broadly refer to the full span of time between the Elden Beast becoming the Elden Ring and when it is Shattered by Marika.

- The Night of Black Knives occured during this time period.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Adel, Baron of Night**, also known as **Gaping Jaw**, is a Nightlord boss in Elden Ring Nightreign, encountered on the third night of the Gaping Jaw Expeditions.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown: Adel was a marvel of the natural world—immense, regal, and unrivaled atop his perch. But when the Night's Tide drenched the old island in azure rain, all life withered and perished. Starved of prey, Adel was consumed by an insatiable, ravening hunger that grew into madness.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.markdown:
He is a monstrous black dragon with a sideways jaw and a bottomless appetite. He harnesses the power of violet-purple lightning during his second phase. As an Everdark Sovereign, Adel moves at light speed and whips up a massive cyclone.

Adel deals Standard damage on all moves during the first phase. During phases two and three, he can also deal Lightning damage. He inflicts heavy Blood Loss buildup on its biting grab attack.

Adel is resistant to Fire, Lightning, and Blood Loss, and fully immune to Madness. He is vulnerable to Scarlet Rot, Frostbite, and Sleep; however, he is particularly affected by Poison damage. When the effect is procced, Adel receives the full sum of the damage-over-time upfront, and the next round of status buildup can be applied sooner than usual. However, Adel creates a Poison hazard by vomiting up the contents of his stomach.

sections.heading: Drops
sections.markdown:
- Night of the Baron (first victory)
- Random Relics
- Murk
- Sovereign Sigils (Everdark Sovereign)

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
- HP (solo): 13,140
- HP (trio): 39,420
- HP (Everdark Sovereign): +25%
- Defense: 100
- Stance: 150
- This boss is vulnerable to a Critical Attack after its stance is broken.
- Cannot be parried
- Vulnerable to Anti-dragon effects
- Weak spot: Head ≈ +50%
- Gains a temporary Attack Power Up effect after finishing a successful grab attack, indicated by a red aura
 - Adel deals 112% damage for 30 seconds; the effect is increased to 115% damage during the Everdark Sovereign phase 3
- Adel is scripted to stagger when Poisoned during Phase 1 only. Poison no longer staggers Adel during Phases 2 and 3.
- Grab attack inflicts heavy Blood Loss buildup and partially restores Adel's HP
- Button-mashing does not help end Adel's grab attacks early

sections.heading: Resistances
sections.markdown:
- Damage Types
 - +0% indicates that a boss is neutral to that damage type.
 - A positive value () indicates bonus damage.
 - A negative value ( ) indicates that a boss is resistant to the damage type.

- Resistances
 - A lower value indicates faster procs of the applicable status effect.
 - The **** symbol denotes full immunity to the status effect.

sections.heading: Moveset
sections.markdown:
- Phase 1: No lightning, staggered by Poison
- Phase 2: Lightning, not staggered by Poison

sections.heading: Everdark Sovereign
sections.markdown:
The Everdark Sovereign version of Adel, Baron of Night begins with Phase 2 and transitions to an empowered "Phase 3" fight. Adel gains jagged purple horns on his left and right jaws and is more challenging, utilizing a fully-upgraded moveset.
- This version of the boss does not have the scripted weakness to Poison because it starts in Phase 2.
- When he reaches 60% HP, Adel teleports uncontrollably, then strikes the earth in a flash of lightning, creating a raging tornado and starting Phase 3.
- Tornado deals Lightning damage to players outside its ring; the eye of the storm is only safe zone.
- The tornado can be passed through, but it deals damage; use Spiritstreams to jump in unscathed.
- Tornado lasts 60 seconds, and has a 60-second cooldown; it can be activated once every 120 seconds.
- The hurtbox of several attacks is expanded during Phase 3.
- Prefers the triple ground pound over single ground pounds during Phase 3.

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.markdown:
- Stack Lightning damage negation.
- Eat nine Stanching Boluses to gain a +9 Resistance to Blood Loss.
- Hurl Fetid Pots from behind, never near the mouth.
- During the second phase, watch for and avoid spots where the lightning will strike.
- Jump right before the delayed lightning eruption to avoid all earthquake attacks.
- When fighting the Everdark Sovereign, use the Spiritstream jumps to enter the eye of the storm from above. They appear simultaneously with the tornado.
- One of Adel's attacks displaces him far from his target. If he leaves the tornado ring, avoid chasing after him.
- Allies can be freed from Adel's biting grab attack by breaking his stance
- Guardian, Raider, and Wylder can survive the full grab attack.
- During Phases 2 and 3, Adel gains access to a variation of the grab that lasts longer and deals additional damage.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- This Nightlord can be challenged after defeating Gladius, Beast of Night for the first time. The Everdark Sovereign Gaping Jaw Expedition is unlocked by beating Adel for the first time.
- Dark Night of the Baron is purchased from the Collector Signboard after defeating the Everdark Sovereign.
- The standard Gaping Jaw Expedition typically features Gaping Dragon or the Crucible Knight and Golden Hippopotamus duo as the second Night bosses. The Everdark Sovereign Expedition has an Ancient Dragon (Phase 1 & 2).

sections.heading: Timeline
sections.markdown:

- Concurrent: Age of the Erdtree

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown: The age of Plenty was a time of bountiful grace and prosperity for the Erdtree civilization at Leyndell, Royal Capital. It was the beginning of Queen Marika's reign as a god.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
When the new age began, the Erdtree flourished with abundance. It secreted primordial life energy in the form of sacred sap, which hardened into an amber that was treasured as the most precious of jewels. These blessings fell like golden tears from its boughs, pooling in flasks or large collection basins. Queen Marika personally bestowed them to her Elden Lord and a chosen few. These Sacred Tears were worshipped and used to spread the faith in churches across all lands.

During these early days, the Erdtree radiated the gentle warmth of the sun and healed all who basked in its golden glow. Its bark at this time was brown, much like the Minor Erdtrees.

It was thought that the blessed sap of the Erdtree would drip from its boughs forever, but that era of blind belief swiftly came to an end. It was only for a fleeting moment, as is the course of all life. Over time, the Erdtree became more an object of faith.

sections.markdown:

- Messmer's Crusade may have occured toward the end of the Age of Plenty.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown: Ancient Bowers are enormous stone trees that are found above and below ground, scattered throughout the Abyssal Woods, Consecrated Snowfield, Mohgwyn Palace, and Siofra River. They are varied in size, though each was large enough to be drawn on the world map, with some individuals rivaling Minor Erdtrees in stature. They are the petrified remains of trees grown long before Queen Marika's Erdtree, likely cultivated by the Ancient Dynasty in times of old, given the sacred tree-tending scenes recorded on nearby Obelisk Beacons. Albinaurics, Ancestral Followers, and Spark Orbs commonly dwell among the ancient bowers.

sections.heading: Locations
sections.markdown:
- Abyssal Woods

- Consecrated Snowfield - a chill forest of ancient trees accented by red flowers and clusters of Rimed Crystal Buds.
- Mohgwyn Palace - petrified stumps, slacked with the Formless Mother's accursed blood, sprout fresh green buds.
- Siofra River
- Worshipper's Woods

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Bloody Wolf** was one of the five playable characters . Unlike the Prophet and Warrior origins, Bloody Wolf, along with Champion and Enchanted Knight, would not appear in the final game.

sections.heading: Recreating
sections.markdown:
Though this class isn't available in the final release of the game, it can be recreated.

The weapon and the shield can be acquired early, as the Bastard Sword is bought from the Nomadic Merchant at the Castle Morne Rampart Site of Grace in the Weeping Peninsula and the Iron Roundshield is bought from the Nomadic Merchant outside of Coastal Cave in western Limgrave.

The Armor Set and the Skill's Ash of War require access to Leyndell, Royal Capital and thus need 2 Great Runes.

 WARNING: Both the Armor Set and the Ash of War becomes inaccessible after defeating Maliketh, the Black Blade unless you start a new Journey.
The Raging Wolf Set requires completion of the first two invasions as part of Tanith's questline at Volcano Manor to gain the Letter to Bernahl and be able to invade Vargram the Raging Wolf and Errant Sorcerer Wilhelm inside of the Fortified Manor in Leyndell, Royal Capital and gain the set.
Ash of War: Thunderbolt meanwhile is dropped by a Teardrop Scarab west-northwest of the Avenue Balcony Site of Grace, in the courtyard hidden under the gigantic wing of Gransax and is guarded by a Black Dumpling Albinauric.

sections.heading: Suitable Origins
sections.markdown:
The Vagabond origin is arguably the most well-suited for this purpose as it has stats that are very similar to the Bloody Wolf's, can wield the Bastard Sword two-handed without any additional stats (and can wield it one-handed with 2 more points in Strength) and the Iron Roundshield one-handed, and wears an armor set of similar weight. It does however need at least 2 more points in Endurance to wield the weapon and the shield with either Armor Set, without even including Talismans.

The Hero origin, while not quite as suited stat-wise and having worse armor, is still decently suitable as it only needs 1 more point in Dexterity to wield the Bastard Sword and can comfortably wield the weapon and shield without having to increase its Endurance.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown:
Astrologer** is one of the starting origins in Elden Ring.

Consider this origin very carefully. While melee and bow fighters are spoiled for choice of weapons and equipment very early on from both loot and stores, you will not get access to effective equipment for spellcasting until you are past at least two major bosses of Margit, the Fell Omen and Godrick the Grafted, where you will be finally able to buy the equipment listed below that the Astrologer starts with. The Sorceress Sellen who will be your main spell teacher is also locked behind a boss fight. Even if you heavily prefer melee or bow combat, it might be worthwhile taking the Astrologer anyways just for the early tactical option of the spells.

When choosing to be an Astrologer i.e. spellcaster, you're going to have to force your "hand preference" and controls based on your intended combat style due to two key spells that hard-force whether your Staff can be in your Right or Left hand, with such spells being blocked from firing in the opposite orientation. Note that the handedness has no effect on the raw strength of spells, nor does 2-handing a staff.

- Scholar's Armament forces you to have the staff in the Left hand in order to be able to enchant a weapon on the Right.
- Scholar's Shield forces you to have the staff in the Right hand in order to be able to enchant a shield on the Left.

Given that you can't have the same staff equipped twice in two different weapon slots and that it is not economical to keep Strengthening two separate staffs as you level up, it is suggested to stick with just one of the above. If you truly detest melee combat except as a last resort and want to stick with spells as much as possible, go with a Right-handed staff to be able to use the shield buff for more defense (which is the Astrologer's default setup when you first start the game). Otherwise, switch the staff to the Left hand and get used to the different activation keys so that you can use the surprisingly powerful weapon buff.

sections.heading: Build Optimization
sections.markdown: For people who wish to select an origin that will have the most optimal stat distribution for a build with the fewest stat points wasted, the Astrologer is the best choice for essentially any build which focuses mainly on Intelligence, and more specifically the Sorceries. Note that these builds are not necessarily "good", they are just what this origin is better at than any other.

sections.heading: Intelligence-Strength-Dex
sections.markdown:
The main goal of this build is to give the Astrologer access to the very powerful spells while simultaneously giving some tactical flexibility in melee and the ability to lure/damage enemies at a range beyond what their spells can reach via a Longbow. If you get your Strength to 20 and Dexterity to 14, you can fully use the Longbow and the Pike, as well as several of the shields that have a 100% Physical damage reduction through guarding like the Heater Shield. However, as an alternate option you can stick with the Pike and Staff build for liberal use of Scholar's Armament, and then you can easily have both spells and melee attacks happening interchangeably along with relying on dodge rolls for defense. In this instance, just remove the shield to reduce your Equip Load; remember that a Shield only helps you, in any way, if you Guard with it. They do not give any bonus passive defenses just from wearing them like Armor does, so you may be better off saving the weight of the Shield and wearing a stronger Armor instead.

You won't really need to push either stat much further than this for a LONG time. Then you can pile on Intelligence, as well as the occasional Vigor, Mind and Endurance for improved HP, FP and Stamina capacity; keep Vigor and Mind up enough so that your HP and FP max capacities are just slightly above what a Flask charge can restore, growing as you upgrade the Flask strength.

Make liberal use of the auto-targeting feature and your range. While not having a particularly fast damage output, Glintstone Pebble is extremely FP-efficient against single targets. Glintstone Arc has identical damage per shot as Pebble but with a higher FP cost and slightly less range, however it can hit small groups of enemies simultaneously which is where it truly shines. Combine these with a careful evasive ranged combat style and a decent Summon, and you can do VERY well for quite some time before you even find another reasonable spell.

Once you've gotten comfortable with the attack patterns of certain enemies you can easily switch to melee with the ultra-long Pike (using the Spear beforehand which is acquired earlier), allowing for efficient kills without burning through too much FP.

One additional benefit of this playstyle is that the equipped weaponry and staves of Magic Users tends to be fairly light, since they can use spell selection to give them a spread of short range and long range combat options. This in turn allows magic users to wear heavier, more protective armor than melee fighters normally would at the same load limit and still maintain good mobility.
